commands.description: LinkedIn account connection management.
List connected LinkedIn accounts.

args.name: external-id
args.description: Only accounts whose external_id (your own end-user id, set on link) equals this value exactly.

commands.description: Get a connected LinkedIn account: its status (active, reconnect_needed, restricted, connecting or disconnected), its per-action quotas (the strict rows carry a target and an effective_target; connection_requests_no_note counts every invitation) and its health (state healthy, watch, slowed or stopped; factor; reasons). Curviate cannot see actions sent by hand or by another tool on the Account. --verbose adds cached profile fields, which may be null.

args.name: account-id
args.description: Account id (acc_...).

commands.description: List the workspace's live seats and whether each is free or bound to an account. A seat with occupied:false (free) is a seat_id `curviate account link --seat-id` accepts right now. Not paginated (bounded by purchased seats), --all is not supported. An empty result can mean the workspace has no seats, or that billing needs attention.

Connect a LinkedIn account to an empty seat. AI agents: do not read, pass or ask for passwords, cookies or cookie exports; run `curviate account connect-request create` and hand the person its link instead. --cookies-file takes an export of a live LinkedIn session; delete it after use. If LinkedIn requires verification you'll be prompted for the code interactively. Given --auth-method and its credentials, a non-interactive shell exits 12 at that step and you finish with `curviate account checkpoint solve <account_id> --code`.

args.name: seat-id
args.description: Empty seat to bind the account to, listed by `curviate account seats` (a free seat there is one this call accepts right now). Omit it and the only free seat is used; with zero or several free the command says so and connects nothing. Required with --preview (which calls nothing) and with --account-id (a reconnect keeps the seat that account already holds).

args.name: auth-method
args.description: Authentication method: credentials | cookie. Not needed with --cookies-file, which implies cookie.

args.name: cookies-file
args.description: The Cookie-Editor JSON export of a signed-in linkedin.com tab: a path, or - to read it from stdin (on a terminal: paste, then Ctrl-D; nothing is shown). The file holds a live LinkedIn session: delete it after use. Only li_at and li_a are sent. Needs --user-agent. Not with --li-at, --li-at-stdin, --li-a, --email, --password or --password-stdin.

args.name: email
args.description: LinkedIn email (credentials method).

args.name: password
args.description: LinkedIn password (credentials method). Note: a value on the command line is visible to other processes via `ps` and saved in shell history; prefer `--password-stdin` or the CURVIATE_LINKEDIN_PASSWORD env var.

args.name: password-stdin
args.description: Read the LinkedIn password from stdin (one line, trimmed).

args.name: li-at
args.description: LinkedIn session cookie li_at (cookie method). Note: a value on the command line is visible to other processes via `ps` and saved in shell history; prefer `--li-at-stdin` or the CURVIATE_LINKEDIN_LI_AT env var.

args.name: li-at-stdin
args.description: Read the li_at session cookie from stdin (one line, trimmed).

args.name: li-a
args.description: Optional premium session cookie li_a (cookie method). Note: a value on the command line is visible to other processes via `ps` and saved in shell history; prefer the CURVIATE_LINKEDIN_LI_A env var.

args.name: country
args.description: Where LinkedIn sees this account connecting from: a two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code (e.g. US, DE; case-insensitive), the country its owner normally signs in from. A new connect needs exactly one of --country, --ip or --proxy-host. Strict: the connect fails rather than use another country, unless --allow-country-fallback.

args.name: ip
args.description: A public IPv4 address whose country becomes the connection location (strict, like --country). An alternative to --country.

args.name: allow-country-fallback
args.description: With --country or --ip: allow a connection from another country when none is free in the chosen one. Without it the connect is strict and fails instead.

args.name: proxy-protocol
args.description: Proxy protocol: http | https | socks5 | socks4.

args.name: proxy-host
args.description: Your own proxy's host or IP. Your proxy decides where LinkedIn sees the account connecting from, so --country, --ip and --allow-country-fallback are not accepted with it.

args.name: proxy-port
args.description: Proxy port.

args.name: proxy-username
args.description: Proxy auth username.

args.name: proxy-password
args.description: Proxy auth password. Note: a value on the command line is visible to other processes via `ps` and saved in shell history; prefer the CURVIATE_PROXY_PASSWORD env var.

args.name: user-agent
args.description: Browser User-Agent to pin for this account. Required with --auth-method cookie: a session cookie only works paired with the User-Agent of the browser it was copied from, and the command exits 2 without it. Optional with --auth-method credentials, where it is still pinned for the account when given.

args.name: recruiter-contract-id
args.description: Recruiter contract to select once the account is connected, so a connected account may still have none selected: `contract_selected: false` in the answer means connected, not selected. Only meaningful when the LinkedIn account holds a Recruiter subscription.

args.name: linkedin-premium
args.description: Narrow this connection to one LinkedIn premium surface: sales_navigator | recruiter. Omit it and the connect asks for every product and LinkedIn activates what the account holds. Applies to THIS call only and is never remembered, so restate it on every connect and reconnect where Recruiter must win.

args.name: products
args.description: Comma-separated premium products to ask for: sales_navigator, recruiter. Omit to ask for both (--linkedin-premium still narrows). Classic LinkedIn and company pages are always included.

args.name: external-id
args.description: Your own id for this account's end user (1-255 chars, not unique). Returned on the account and every account webhook; filter with `curviate account list --external-id`. Use an opaque id, not an email.

args.name: timezone
args.description: Ignored: the account's time zone follows its connection location. Accepted so existing scripts keep working; nothing is sent.

args.name: warm-up
args.description: --warm-up connects the new account with warm-up on: its limits start at 30% and rise to full by day 14 of its sending days (the Gradual ramp). Default off (full limits from the start); --no-warm-up is accepted and changes nothing. A new connect only; for a connected account use `curviate account warm-up`.

args.name: account-id
args.description: Existing account id (acc_...) to re-authenticate IN PLACE. Passing it makes this an in-place reconnect of that account. Omit to connect a NEW account into --seat-id.

args.name: no-interactive
args.description: Never prompt for a checkpoint code. On a checkpoint, always render the envelope and exit 12, even on a TTY.

examples: curviate account link --auth-method credentials --email jane@example.com --password-stdin --country US
curviate account link --auth-method credentials --email jane@example.com --password-stdin --account-id acc_YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID --seat-id SEAT_ID
curviate account link --cookies-file linkedin-cookies.json --user-agent "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36" --country US
requires: Exactly one of --country, --ip or --proxy-host on a new connect; a reconnect (--account-id) may omit it to keep the account's location.
--seat-id with --preview or --account-id, and when zero or several seats are free.
--password-stdin only with --auth-method credentials; --li-at-stdin only with --auth-method cookie.

rules.changes: Connects a LinkedIn account to a seat, signing in with the credentials or session cookies you pass; with --account-id, signs an existing Account in again.
rules.visible_to: Your Team gets the Account to operate; LinkedIn sees a sign-in from the chosen location.
rules.retry: Not safe for a new connect: each success takes another seat. Read `curviate account list` first.
rules.undo: `curviate account disconnect <account_id>` disconnects it and releases the seat.
rules.blast_radius: One LinkedIn account and one seat.

errors.ACCOUNT_ALREADY_LINKED: this LinkedIn account is already connected: reconnect it with --account-id.
errors.CONNECTION_IN_PROGRESS: a connect for this seat is still running.
errors.LINKEDIN_AUTH_FAILED: LinkedIn did not accept the credentials or cookies.
errors.CONNECTION_LOCATION_REQUIRED: a new connect named no location.

commands.description: Connect a LinkedIn account without any credential passing through you: create a request, give the person its link, read it until done.

Ask a person to connect a new LinkedIn account, or with --reconnect to reconnect one, without handing you any credential. Prints the link to give them; they connect in their own Curviate dashboard, where the request is also listed. The link expires if it is not opened in time. AI agents: never ask for, read or pass a LinkedIn password, cookies or verification codes. Use this instead.

args.name: reconnect
args.description: Reconnect this account (acc_...) instead of connecting a new one.

args.name: warm-up
args.description: --warm-up: the new account starts with warm-up on once the person connects it (limits at 30%, rising to full by day 14 of its sending days). Default off (full limits from the start); --no-warm-up is accepted and changes nothing. A new connect only.

rules.changes: Creates a pending connect request and a link. Nothing is connected until the person completes it.
rules.visible_to: Your Team: the person it is for sees it listed under Accounts in their dashboard.
rules.retry: Not safe: a repeated call creates a second request. Read `curviate account connect-request get <request_id>` first.
rules.undo: `curviate account connect-request cancel <request_id>`.

errors.ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND: --reconnect names an account that is unknown, archived or another Team's.
errors.INSUFFICIENT_ROLE: your role cannot operate the account you named.
errors.ACCOUNT_NOT_SHARED: the account you named is not shared with you.

commands.description: Read a connect request: pending, completed (with the connected account_id, or mailbox_id for a Mailbox request), expired, failed or cancelled. Poll it until it leaves pending. A Mailbox request (kind mailbox_connect or mailbox_reconnect, from `curviate mailbox connect` or `reconnect`) also carries mailbox_id and, where the provider needs one, admin_consent_url.

args.name: id
args.description: Connect request id (creq_...), LinkedIn account or Mailbox.

output: The request: status, and account_id (or mailbox_id) once completed; error_code when the last attempt failed. Never a credential, code or the step the person is on.

commands.description: Cancel a pending connect request, a LinkedIn account's or a Mailbox's; its link stops working. A request that is no longer pending is refused.

args.name: id
args.description: Connect request id (creq_...), LinkedIn account or Mailbox.

rules.changes: The request becomes cancelled and its link stops working.
rules.visible_to: Your Team: it leaves the person's Accounts list.
rules.retry: Safe: cancelling a cancelled request answers the same request again.
rules.undo: Cannot be undone; create a new request.

errors.CONNECT_REQUEST_NOT_PENDING: the request is completed, expired or failed; the message names which.
errors.CONNECT_REQUEST_IN_USE: the person is completing it right now; try again in a minute.
errors.RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND: no such request, or it was removed a day after it ended.

commands.description: In-progress connect operations (poll for completion).

Poll the status of an in-progress connect (auth intent) for completion. Without --wait: a single poll. The JSON `status` field (pending | resolved | expired | failed) tells you what to do next. With --wait: block on the same adaptive cadence as `curviate account link` until a terminal state.

args.name: timeout
args.description: Wait-loop timeout in milliseconds (requires --wait; default: time remaining to the session's expiry). Note the unit: this is milliseconds.

args.name: session
args.description: The account's acc_... id, returned by `curviate account link` or a checkpoint response.

args.name: wait
args.description: Poll on an adaptive cadence (1000ms, then 1500ms for 30s, then 3000ms) until a terminal state, instead of a single poll.

rules.changes: Asks for the status of a connect that is still running; with --wait, keeps asking until it ends.
rules.visible_to: Your Team; a connect that finishes makes the Account available.
rules.retry: Safe: it only asks again.
rules.undo: Nothing to undo; a connected Account is released with `curviate account disconnect <account_id>`.

errors.CONNECTION_IN_PROGRESS: the connect has not ended yet.

commands.description: Update an account's metadata, connection location, own proxy or whether its Connections are saved as Leads. Prints the updated account, with connection_location re-read after a location change.

args.name: account-id
args.description: Account id (acc_...).

args.name: metadata
args.description: Custom metadata as a JSON object (flat string->string map). Replaces the store wholesale. Example: '{"team":"growth"}'.

args.name: country
args.description: Move this account's connection location to this two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code (e.g. US, DE). LinkedIn sees a new IP there and may ask the owner to verify, so change it only when the current location is wrong. Strict unless --allow-country-fallback. On an account using your own proxy, pass --clear-proxy with it.

args.name: allow-country-fallback
args.description: Allow a connection from another country when none is free in the chosen one. Alone, it changes the strictness of the configured country; --no-allow-country-fallback makes it strict.

args.name: clear-proxy
args.description: Stop using your own proxy and return to a managed location. Requires --country. Mutually exclusive with --proxy-host.

args.name: proxy-protocol
args.description: Proxy protocol: http | https | socks5 | socks4.

args.name: proxy-host
args.description: Your own proxy's host or IP. Not accepted with --country.

args.name: proxy-port
args.description: Proxy port.

args.name: proxy-username
args.description: Proxy auth username.

args.name: proxy-password
args.description: Proxy auth password. Note: a value on the command line is visible to other processes via `ps` and saved in shell history; prefer the CURVIATE_PROXY_PASSWORD env var.

args.name: save-connections-as-leads
args.description: Save this account's Connections as Leads (Automate; on by default): each person becomes one Lead in your team, do-not-contact people skipped. Turning it on also saves the Connections already synced; --no-save-connections-as-leads stops it and keeps the Leads saved so far.

rules.changes: Changes the Account's metadata, connection location, own proxy or Save Connections as Leads.
rules.visible_to: Your Team; LinkedIn sees the new location and may ask the owner to verify.
rules.retry: Safe: the same values written again leave the Account the same.
rules.undo: Run it again with the previous values; metadata is replaced wholesale and the old map is not kept.

errors.ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND: the Account is not in your Team.
errors.CONNECTION_LOCATION_UNAVAILABLE: no connection is free in that country.

commands.description: Hard-disconnect a LinkedIn account and release its seat.

args.name: account-id
args.description: Account id (acc_...).

rules.changes: The Account is disconnected and deleted from Curviate, its seat is released, and its stored data goes with it.
rules.visible_to: Everyone using this workspace's key: the Account disappears from `curviate account list`. Nothing is posted on LinkedIn.
rules.retry: A retry after success answers ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND; read `curviate account list` first.
rules.undo: Cannot be undone. Link the LinkedIn account again with `curviate account link`; history does not come back.
rules.blast_radius: One Account and everything stored for it.

errors.ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND: no Account with this id (already disconnected, or another workspace's).

commands.description: Checkpoint challenge operations (solve with an OTP, poll mobile-app approval, or re-request the challenge notification).
Solve a checkpoint challenge with an OTP / 2FA code.

args.name: account-id
args.description: The provisional account_id (acc_...) from the 202 checkpoint_required response.

args.name: code
args.description: The OTP / 2FA verification code.

rules.changes: Sends the verification code for the Account's pending checkpoint; on success the Account connects.
rules.visible_to: LinkedIn, and your Team once the Account is connected.
rules.retry: Read `curviate account get <account_id>` first: a wrong code counts against the attempts the checkpoint allows.
rules.undo: Nothing to undo; disconnect with `curviate account disconnect <account_id>`.

errors.CHECKPOINT_NOT_FOUND: the Account has no pending checkpoint.
errors.CHECKPOINT_MAX_ATTEMPTS: too many wrong codes: connect again.

commands.description: Poll for mobile-app approval of a pending checkpoint challenge. With --wait, blocks on an adaptive cadence until a terminal state (or --timeout elapses) instead of a single poll.

args.name: timeout
args.description: Wait-loop timeout in milliseconds (requires --wait; default: time remaining to the checkpoint's expiry).

args.name: account-id
args.description: The provisional account_id (acc_...) from the 202 checkpoint_required response.

args.name: wait
args.description: Poll on an adaptive cadence (1000ms, then 1500ms for 30s, then 3000ms) until a terminal state, instead of a single poll.

rules.changes: Asks LinkedIn whether the mobile-app approval has happened; with --wait, keeps asking until it ends.
rules.visible_to: LinkedIn, and your Team once the Account is connected.
rules.retry: Safe: it only asks again.
rules.undo: Nothing to undo; disconnect with `curviate account disconnect <account_id>`.

errors.CHECKPOINT_NOT_FOUND: the Account has no pending checkpoint.

commands.description: Re-request the challenge notification for a pending checkpoint (e.g. re-send an OTP email, SMS code, or mobile-app approval push). Not every challenge type supports it; an authenticator- app code has nothing to re-send. The response's `resent` boolean tells you honestly whether a new notification actually went out; the command still exits 0 either way. With --challenge it instead answers a challenge_selection checkpoint by picking the verification method.

args.name: account-id
args.description: The provisional account_id (acc_...) from the 202 checkpoint_required response.

args.name: challenge
args.description: Answer a challenge_selection checkpoint: an id from its challenges list (email | sms | whatsapp). Prints the next checkpoint and exits 12; solve it with `curviate account checkpoint solve`. Omit to re-send the current code.

examples: curviate account checkpoint request acc_YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID --challenge sms

rules.changes: Asks LinkedIn to send the challenge notification again, or with --challenge picks the verification method.
rules.visible_to: The Account's owner, who receives a new code or push.
rules.retry: A repeat sends another notification; the answer's `resent` says whether one went out.
rules.undo: Cannot be undone: the notification is sent.

errors.CHECKPOINT_NOT_FOUND: the Account has no pending checkpoint.

commands.description: One Account's overview over a window: profile and status, latest metrics, outcomes so far (acceptance, reply, InMail reply), budget rows used today, its Campaigns, and flags with the next command to run. Each Lead counts once per Account.

args.name: accountId
args.description: The Account (acc_...).

args.name: from
args.description: First day, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, in --timezone. A Campaign read (with or without --campaign) or an Account overview may start more than a year back: up to `window.counts_only_through` the figures come from daily counts (UTC days, no step, variant or seen detail), and `paths` cover only the days after `window.paths_through`. --view activity and the activity exports keep their own cap, named in the refusal.

args.name: to
args.description: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, in --timezone (default today). Same rules as --from.

args.name: range
args.description: Instead of --from/--to: 7d, 30d, 90d, 12m or all.

args.name: timezone
args.description: IANA zone the days are read in (default UTC).

args.name: bucket
args.description: Daily series grouping: auto, day, week or month.

args.name: campaigns
args.description: Only these Campaigns, comma list (mot_...).

args.name: origin
args.description: Who sent the actions: a comma list of campaign, unibox, api; direct is an alias for unibox and api.

args.name: include
args.description: Sections to return, comma list (for example performance,campaigns,accounts,steps,variants,paths,flags). forecast: what your Campaigns are expected to send and get per day from today, a simulation with their observed rates; Campaigns only, the configuration frozen as it is now (no new Enrollments, no edits), never in the summary.

args.name: forecast-days
args.description: With --include forecast: days after today, 1-365 (default 30); the forecast ends sooner when activity does.

args.name: sort
args.description: Order of the Campaign and Account lists, comma list of sent, acceptance.rate, reply.rate, inmail_reply.rate, last_activity_at, name; a leading - sorts descending.

args.name: limit
args.description: How many Campaigns and Accounts to return.

args.name: compare
args.description: previous_period: add the same number of days before --from to every rate (`previous`, `delta`).

output: A compact table by default; --json (or piped) prints the API body.

commands.description: One Account's daily profile metrics, one row per day: connections, followers, profile viewers (90 days), search appearances (week), post impressions (7 days), SSI and its pillars.

args.name: accountId
args.description: The Account (acc_...).

args.name: from
args.description: First day, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, in --timezone.

args.name: to

args.description: IANA zone the days are read in (default UTC).

commands.description: Turn an Account's warm-up ramp on or off.

Turn the Account's warm-up on: its limits ramp from now in its sending days, Gradual (30% on day 1 to 100% on day 14) or Custom (--start percent on day 1, plus --step points every --every sending days). Prints the resulting warm-up.

args.name: accountId
args.description: The Account (acc_...).

args.name: preset
args.description: gradual (default: 30% on day 1 to 100% on day 14) or custom.

args.name: start
args.description: Custom: the percentage on day 1, 5 to 90.

args.name: step
args.description: Custom: percentage points added each time, 1 to 50.

args.name: every
args.description: Custom: sending days between steps, 1 to 7.

examples: curviate account warm-up on acc_YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID --preset custom --start 20 --step 10 --every 2

rules.changes: The Account's warm-up switch is set on; every budget row's effective ceiling follows.
rules.visible_to: Everyone using this workspace's key. Nothing is posted on LinkedIn.
rules.retry: Safe to repeat: the switch ends in the same state.
rules.undo: Run `curviate account warm-up off <account>`.
rules.blast_radius: One Account's pace.

commands.description: Turn the Account's warm-up off (the default): full limits at once; recovery after a LinkedIn restriction still applies. Prints the resulting warm-up.

args.name: accountId
args.description: The Account (acc_...).

rules.changes: The Account's warm-up switch is set off; every budget row's effective ceiling follows.
rules.visible_to: Everyone using this workspace's key. Nothing is posted on LinkedIn.
rules.retry: Safe to repeat: the switch ends in the same state.
rules.undo: Run `curviate account warm-up on <account>`.
rules.blast_radius: One Account's pace.

commands.description: Read or change one Account's safety policy (limits per budget row, Active hours, the Activity level), read its limit hits (events), or with --team your Team's email defaults.

With --team, the Team's own policy: its defaults per limit profile and budget row and `email` (default_daily_cap, opt_out_scope and the three opt-out texts in force, the shipped default when none is set). Otherwise one Account's safety policy: every budget row with its ceiling, effective_ceiling and (strict rows) target and effective_target, Active hours, warm-up, pacing, auto_withdraw and the Activity level (activity_level, and activity_level_effective with activity_level_reason when it runs lower). A read: no LinkedIn call.

args.name: team
args.description: The Team's safety policy instead of one Account's: pass --team alone for the Team your key or profile names, or --team tnt_... for another of your Teams. Not with an Account id.

args.name: accountId
args.description: The Account (acc_...). Not with --team.

examples: curviate account safety get acc_YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID --fields active_hours,warm_up

commands.description: With --team, change the Team's email defaults instead, with the --email-* flags: the daily cap a new Mailbox gets (--email-default-cap, at most 50), what an opt-out covers (--email-opt-out-scope everything|email_only) and the three opt-out texts every email step carries (--email-opt-out-text up to 200 characters, --email-opt-out-link-text up to 100, --email-opt-out-link-word up to 30; one plain line, no variables; "" restores the shipped default). Prints the Team policy. commands.description: Store a Draft. Every part is optional. With --schedule-at (and an account and text) Curviate publishes it at that time. Each account, and the no-account bucket, has a Draft limit and a media quota (DRAFT_LIMIT_REACHED, MEDIA_QUOTA_EXCEEDED). A retry creates a second Draft. Needs Automate.

args.name: account
args.description: Account the Draft publishes as (acc_...). Never defaulted: omit it for a Draft with no account yet.

args.name: text
args.description: Post text (up to 3000 characters). Pass - to read from stdin.

args.name: schedule-at
args.description: Publish at this time: ISO 8601 with an offset (e.g. 2026-10-12T09:00:00+02:00), passed through unchanged. A time in the future, not too close to another scheduled Draft on the same account (SCHEDULE_CONFLICT). Needs an account and text.

args.name: attach
args.description: File to attach, repeatable; keeps the order given. Several images (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP), or one MP4 video, or one PDF, never mixed. A file over its size limit is refused.

examples: curviate core draft create "Three things we learned shipping our first agent integration."
curviate core draft create "Launch day." --account acc_YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID --schedule-at 2026-10-12T09:00:00+02:00
curviate core draft create "Demo." --account acc_YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID --attach screenshot.png
